_readme: Template profile. `bin/factory add-project <name> --repo <path>` copies this folder to projects/<name>/ and fills in repo, base_branch and ports. Keys starting with _ are comments. Any key from engine/defaults.json (routing, surfaces, models, max_rounds, timeouts) can be overridden here.
_repo: path: the project's git checkout (absolute). remote: its origin URL; `bin/factory run` run inside that repo finds this profile by it.
_base_branch: Jobs branch from it, and reviews and the gate compare against it.
_pull_base: Before each new job the factory fetches base_branch from origin and fast-forwards it if it is strictly behind. It never merges, rebases or pushes; if it can't (offline, no origin, ahead, diverged, a dirty checkout in the way), the job starts from the local branch and the reason goes to the job's events.log. false turns this off.
_delivery: What happens to an approved job. handoff (default): it ends as an approved branch in your repo; you push it and open a pull request, the project's usual way. next_steps, if set, replaces the suggested commands ({branch}, {base}, {repo}, {job} are filled in). local-merge: merge into base_branch locally with no person looking, only where that is allowed; strategy is merge, squash or rebase. Nothing is ever pushed.
_protected_paths: The gate fails a branch that modifies, renames or deletes an existing file matching these. Adding files is fine. fnmatch patterns where * also matches /; a trailing / means a whole folder.
_spec_may_unlock_protected: When a requested change makes an existing protected test wrong, the spec writer may list that file under `## Protected changes`; the gate then lets the builder change exactly that file, and code review checks the change. false keeps protected files untouchable, which sends such jobs to you instead.
_ports: The builder uses base, reviewers base+1, base+2, … when they start a dev server.
_commands: setup runs once in each new worktree. The others are shown to agents in their briefs; in dev, {port} stands for the agent's own port. Leave a command empty if the project has none.
_browser: A CLI agents can use to look at pages (for example agent-browser). Empty means none.
